name: K18 peptide
lead: K18 is a branded hair-repair ingredient, a short synthetic peptide sold in leave-in treatment masks and related products from the haircare brand K18. It is used after shampooing on bleached, dyed, heat-styled or otherwise damaged hair, with the aim of leaving strands stronger, smoother and shinier so the hair looks healthier, holds volume and styles better, and breaks less.[1][2]

The brand describes the peptide as modelled on keratin, the main structural protein of hair, and says it works inside the strand to restore damaged polypeptide chains. Beauty writers explain it as peptides that help stitch broken hair bonds back together, and set it alongside bond-building treatments such as Olaplex, whose patented ingredient is described as targeting broken disulfide bonds. These mechanism statements come from the brand and press coverage.[1][2][3]

Treatments are typically applied to towel-dried, shampooed hair without conditioner, left on for around four minutes and then styled as usual. One beauty editor reviewing it on bleached, dyed hair reported that hair felt instantly thicker and stronger and kept volume, while softness and frizz control fell short of what she wanted; she described it as most useful for very damaged hair with split ends.[2]

angle.text: K18 is used to improve how damaged hair looks and feels: stronger, fuller-feeling and less prone to breakage after bleaching or heat styling, so colour-treated hair can be kept longer and look healthier. It is a rinse-free leave-in applied from roots to ends, usually before styling.

infobox: After shampoo, no conditioner, about four minutes[2]

paras: K18 products contain a proprietary peptide the company calls the K18 peptide, marketed for repairing hair damaged by bleaching, colouring, chemical straightening and heat. The pitch is that it acts inside the hair shaft rather than coating it. [1][2]

The name is a brand identifier. In scientific literature, abbreviations such as K18 refer to unrelated things, for example the tau protein fragment K18 or keratin 18 in epithelial cells, which have no connection to the haircare ingredient.

In appearance communities K18 is discussed as a repair step for people who bleach or heat-style their hair, and is often compared with Olaplex in price and results. Both are described as bond-focused repair treatments, with K18 priced higher.[1] Olaplex, founded in 2014, says its products rebuild broken bonds in hair damaged by chemical, thermal and mechanical stress; Wikipedia reports that a 2023 lawsuit by 28 women alleged that Olaplex products caused hair damage and hair loss, and that a proposed class action was rejected.[3]

One published review describes washing with a bond-repair shampoo, skipping conditioner, working a pump and a half of the mask through towel-dried hair from root to tip, leaving it for just over four minutes, then adding a hair oil and rough-drying.[2] Some guides suggest pairing it with a pre-shampoo bonding treatment.[2]

No studies found of the K18 haircare product. Published peptide research under the label K18 concerns unrelated molecules, such as tau fragments, keratin 18 in epithelial cells and a histone lysine.[4][5]
K18 is a cosmetic and sold over the counter. As with any hair product, scalp or skin irritation or allergy is possible, and product labels advise following the directions for use.

lore.intro: K18 is discussed in beauty press and hair communities mainly as a premium repair mask, frequently compared with Olaplex.

claims.claim: K18 repairs broken keratin chains inside the hair
claims.believers: The brand says its peptide mimics keratin's structure and repairs damaged polypeptide bonds, and reviewers describe it as stitching broken bonds back together and report stronger-feeling hair.[1][2]
claims.experts: The mechanism is a brand-level claim; no independent published trial of the K18 product was found.

claims.claim: K18 gives results similar to Olaplex at a higher price
claims.believers: Reviewers describe both as leaving hair smooth and shiny, with K18 priced higher.
claims.experts: Comparisons are editorial reviews rather than controlled studies; Olaplex's ingredient is described in Wikipedia as targeting disulfide bonds, a different bond from the one K18 says it reconnects.[1][3]

claims.claim: K18 makes damaged hair stronger but its smoothness effect varies
claims.believers: A beauty editor reported hair that felt thicker and stronger with long-lasting volume, and better resilience while straightening.[2]
claims.experts: She also reported that it was not particularly soft or frizz-free on her bleached hair, and preferred other products for texture and shine; no controlled trial has tested the product.[2]

card.summary: A branded keratin-mimicking peptide leave-in mask used to make bleached or heat-damaged hair look and feel stronger, smoother and shinier.
card.aka: K18 Leave-In Molecular Repair Hair Mask, K18Hair

quick.overview:
K18 is a leave-in hair treatment built around a branded peptide. People use it after shampooing to help damaged, bleached or heat-styled hair look smoother and shinier.

It is often compared with Olaplex No. 3, usually at a higher price per millilitre.
quick.mechanism: The brand says the peptide imitates keratin and reconnects broken polypeptide chains within the hair shaft. Application is a few minutes on towel-dried hair with no conditioner.
quick.risks: It is an over-the-counter cosmetic. Irritation or allergy is possible as with any hair product, and the repair mechanism is described by the brand and reviewers rather than in published trials.
